newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares turn higher in late trade on US data.
newsitem.headline: German shares turn higher in late trade on US data.

text.p: German shares closed late electronic trade at record levels on Thursday after a spate of U.S. economic data finally managed to ease lingering investor fears of a credit tightening in the United States .
The DAX 30 index of leading German shares had earlier closed 13.71 points lower at 2,892.63 as Wall Street's earlier overnight losses weighed on the market.

News of a rise in German jobless to record levels and continued modest economic growth prompted some commentators to renew hopes of a cut in German interest rates, but the impact was not enough to have a meaningful effect on shares.
The main momemtum only came later in the day after the publication of U.S. December producer prices and the latest U.S. weekly jobless figures.

Dealers said the jobless figures in particular, which showed a higher than expected 361,000 claims, had helped the market higher. "People are still cautious but a bit more relaxed now," said one trader.
The IBIS DAX finally closed at 2,936.69, 32.61 points or 1.12 percent up on the day, after earlier setting a new record of 2,937.78. March DAX futures rose 33.0 points to 2,951.5.

The share market was further boosted by the positive reaction by German Bunds to U.S. November wholesale inventories, which rose 0.1 percent compared to the forecast 0.2 percent, while the dollar continued to be strong.
"The exporters are continuing to benefit from that," said a dealer. The U.S. currency held firm throughout the day at slightly above its European open of 1.575 marks.

Traders said U.S. December payrolls, due on Friday at 1330 GMT, would provide the next focus for the market and that it was likely that German shares would again take their lead from the U.S. and domestic debt markets.

Carmaker Volkswagen was the star performer of the day, rising 28.60 marks to a new all-time high of 708.50 after a VW supervisory board source said it had approved the idea of a settlement in its dispute with General Motors.

Legal sources had earlier said they saw an imminent deal in the case of alleged industrial espionage by former GM executives that moved to VW as possible, while GM said it had moderated its stance on possible damages it would seek from VW.
Engineering group Siemens rose after sources said it would combine its fossil fuel activities with those of U.S.-based Westinghouse.
Siemens, whose shares gained 1.29 marks to 77.99, also said was terminating its consumer electronics business because it had not been producing satisfactory results.
Software group SAP traded 9.50 marks higher at 227 marks as dealers said its price had been forced up by a large buy order.
